Events.title: Events
Events.lede: Each event is one record and one purchase. Every event has an invitation with a response form, so you can track and manage your guests.
Events.emptyAll: No events yet. Pick a template to start your first invitation.
Events.emptyActive: Nothing live yet. Pick a template to start your first invitation.
Events.emptyDrafts: No drafts waiting. Saved-but-unpaid invitations land here.
Events.emptyPast: No past events yet. Invitations move here the day after the event.
Events.groupActive: Active — the invitation is live or ready to share
Events.groupDraft: Drafts — not paid for, never reachable
Events.groupPast: Past — closed, kept until the deletion date

Event.noDesign: Pick a design for this invitation first
Event.nothingShared: Nothing shared yet — the reply form opens when the page becomes reachable.
Event.hiddenNote: Only you can see the invitation.
Event.publicNote: Anyone with the link can see the invitation and reply, even people you didn't invite. They'll also see the event's address, date and any other detail you add.
Event.protectedNote: Guests need a password to see the invitation, so only people you share it with see it. The password is printed on the card under the link.
Event.barAria: Replies: {attending} attending and {declined} declined, of {expected} expected guests
Event.seatingPaidOnly: Seating charts come with paid invitations
Event.dataDeletedOn: Guest data was deleted on {date}, {days} days after the event.

Invitations.title: Invitations
Invitations.lede: The guest-facing page of each event — its wording, its design and its printable card. To change the event itself, go to Events.
Invitations.groupActive: Active — the invitation is visible to guests
Invitations.groupDraft: Drafts — hidden or not paid for, never reachable
Invitations.groupPast: Past — closed, kept until the deletion date
Invitations.emptyAll: No invitations yet. Pick a template to start your first one.
Invitations.emptyActive: Nothing visible to guests yet. An invitation goes live once it is paid for and no longer hidden.
Invitations.emptyDrafts: No drafts waiting. Hidden and unpaid invitations land here.
Invitations.emptyPast: No past invitations yet. They move here the day after the event.

free.name: Free
free.blurb: A fixed template with a minimal RSVP form. No seating chart.

standard.name: Standard
standard.blurb: A fixed template with a minimal RSVP form, and a seating chart included.
standard.upsell: Adds a seating chart to this invitation. You pay the difference, and nothing you have written is lost.

custom.name: Custom
custom.blurb: Modular invitation and RSVP sections, template customisation, and a seating chart.
custom.upsell: Unlocks modular sections, your own palette and fonts, and custom RSVP questions. You pay the difference, and nothing you have written is lost.

EventPage.closedBody: Event and invitation editing closed the day before the event. The record stays readable, and your printable file is still yours to download.
EventPage.closingBody: Event and invitation editing close on {date}, the day before the event.
EventPage.repliesClosingBody: The reply form closes on {date}, {custom, select, yes {the time you set} other {the day before the event}}.
EventPage.repliesClosedBody: The reply form closed {custom, select, yes {at the time you set} other {the day before the event}}. You can still add replies that reach you in any other way.
EventPage.unpaidBody: The {tier} edition costs {price}. The page stays hidden and the RSVP form stays closed until payment clears.
EventPage.hiddenBody: Nobody can open the page, not even a guest holding the link, and no reply can arrive. Set the visibility to Public or Protected below once you are ready to share it.
EventPage.unmatchedTitle: {count, plural, one {# unmatched reply} other {# unmatched replies}}
EventPage.unmatchedBody: They are tagged UNKNOWN until you add them or match them to a name someone mistyped.
EventPage.pausedBody: An unusually high number of guests replied compared to the number you expected. If they're real, raise the number to reopen the form. If not, report it.
EventPage.nearExpectedBody: {replied} of the {expected} guests you expect have replied. If more are coming, raise the expected number.
EventPage.overExpectedBody: {replied} guests have replied, but you expected {expected}. Raise the expected number to keep your numbers accurate.

EventEditor.eventNameHint: Your own label for this event. The only place a guest meets it is the browser tab title.
EventEditor.occasionHint: Sets which templates Festio offers first.
EventEditor.languageHint: What your guests read — the reply form, Festio's own wording, and the date. It has nothing to do with the language you read Festio in.
EventEditor.dateHint: The date of your event, and the one shown on the invitation.
EventEditor.languageWarning: Guests who open your link from now on will find the reply form in the new language. Replies already sent are unaffected — they are stored against the question, not its wording. A printable you have already downloaded keeps the language it was made in; download it again to get the new one.
EventEditor.dateWarning: Your invitation will show the new date, but Festio will not tell your guests — that part is yours to do. {count, plural, =0 {No one has replied for this event yet.} one {# guest has already replied for this event.} other {# guests have already replied for this event.}}
EventEditor.closeEarlyNote: Replies close on {date} — the day before the event. Switch this on to close sooner.
EventEditor.closeTooLate: Pick a time no later than the 24-hour cut-off.
EventEditor.closesEarlyNote: Your own time, ahead of the cut-off.
EventEditor.freezeNote: Event and invitation editing close the day before the event.
EventEditor.deletionNote: For GDPR reasons, guest and event data are kept only {days} days after the event date.
EventEditor.expectedTooLow: {count, plural, one {You already have # reply.} other {You already have # replies.}} You can't expect fewer guests than have already replied.
EventEditor.expectedRequired: Enter how many guests you expect.
EventEditor.slugTooShort: Use at least {min} characters — letters, digits and hyphens.
EventEditor.slugReserved: This word is reserved by Festio. Try another.
EventEditor.passwordInvalid: Use at least 4 letters or digits.
EventEditor.addressHint: If you have already shared the link, changing it will break every copy your guests are holding.
EventEditor.addressWarning: The old link stops working the moment you save. Every copy your {count, plural, one {# guest is holding} other {# guests are holding}} leads nowhere, and passing on the new one is yours to do.
EventEditor.passwordWarning: The old password stops working the moment you save. Guests will not be able to see the invitation until you give them the new one.
EventEditor.noindex: For your privacy, no invitation can be found by searching Google or any other search engine, whatever visibility you choose.
EventEditor.expected: How many guests do you expect?
EventEditor.expectedHint: We use this to show how your replies are coming in, and to protect you from spam: if far more replies come in than you expected, we'll pause the form. You can raise the number anytime.
EventEditor.preloadedNote: Match incoming replies against a list of names you expect. Anything that doesn't match is tagged UNKNOWN for you to sort out.
EventEditor.preloadedCount: {count, plural, one {Currently # name on your pre-loaded list} other {Currently # names on your pre-loaded list}}
EventEditor.payNote: Clears the draft for sharing. Visibility stays where you set it until you change it yourself.
EventEditor.deletedBody: The invitation, every reply and any image you uploaded go automatically, {days} days after {date}. Your account is not affected.
EventEditor.deletedBodyPast: The invitation, every reply and any image you uploaded went automatically, {days} days after {date}. Your account is not affected.
EventEditor.keepTitle: Save what you want to keep
EventEditor.keepBody: Export the guest list, every reply, your seating chart and the printable invitation before then. Once the record is deleted it is gone from Festio for good — we have no way to bring it back.
EventEditor.keepBodyPast: Anything not exported before that date is gone from Festio for good — we have no way to bring it back.
EventEditor.controller: Festio only processes this event's data for you, under the <link>DPA in the Terms</link>. What your guests tell you is theirs: use it to run this event and nothing else, never sell it or pass it to anyone who is not helping you host, and keep any copy you download to yourself.
EventEditor.told: The reply form names you as the person responsible for their details, and says what is collected and how long it is kept.
EventEditor.pastBody: There is nothing left to cancel. The record disappears on its own at the deletion date above.
EventEditor.cancelBody: Closes the RSVP form and replaces the invitation with a short message from you. {count, plural, =0 {No guest has replied yet.} one {# guest has already replied and will not be notified.} other {# guests have already replied and none of them will be notified.}} Guest and event data are kept for another {days} days, and you can reopen the event at any point in that window.
EventEditor.cancelled: Event cancelled — the invitation now shows your message
EventEditor.draftBody: Nobody has seen this page and nothing has been paid for, so it can be removed outright. The address is released and cannot be claimed again.
EventEditor.acknowledge: I understand — telling my guests is up to me.
EventEditor.stateLocked: Editing closed — nothing here can be changed
EventEditor.statePending: {count, plural, one {Tick the box in the warning above to save} other {Tick the box in all # warnings above to save}}
EventEditor.saved: Changes saved — your guests were not notified

HostEditor.saved: Invitation saved — your guests were not notified
HostEditor.exported: Your printable is on its way — not yet, though
HostEditor.dateHint: Set with your event details — edit it there to change the date itself.

PrintPanel.tinted: Use matching color for the back and inside of the card.

flat: You will download two images: one for the front, one for the back.
Print them on the two sides of a single sheet of paper — nothing to fold.
Paper size: anything between A6 (smallest recommended) and A5 (largest recommended), as long as you keep the A-series proportions.
folded: You will download two images: one for each side of the sheet.
Print them on the two sides of a single sheet, then fold it in half — the front of the invitation ends up on the outside.
Paper size before folding: anything between A5 (smallest recommended) and A4 (largest recommended), as long as you keep the A-series proportions.
